sources.fact: Indonesia, WhatsApp: 92.7% of internet users aged 16 and above said they used WhatsApp at least once in the past month. Source survey is GWI, Q2 2026, and WhatsApp is the top platform (Instagram 84.0%, TikTok 81.0%, Facebook 79.5%). This is a survey share, not a count.
sources.publisher: DataReportal (author Simon Kemp; analysis by Manochi; copyright Kepios; supported by Meltwater and We Are Social; survey data from GWI)
sources.quote: SELF-DECLARED SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORM USE ... [WhatsApp] 92.7% ... SOURCE: GWI (Q2 2026).
sources.notes: The value appears only in the chart labels. The body text says each bar is the share of internet users 'aged 16 and above' who used the platform 'at least once' during the past month. The chart warns of 'CHANGES IN AUDIENCE COMPOSITION AND SURVEY METHODOLOGY', so do not draw a trend against earlier editions. The body adds that the values may not match platform ad reach data. The same page gives 231 million internet users and 80.2% penetration (October 2026), though the text calls this 'the end of 2026'. The page has no email data at all. The search index carries the same 92.7%. Prior edition: Digital 2026 Indonesia (5 Nov 2025) gave 230 million users and a population of 286 million; its WhatsApp value was not in the page text.

sources.fact: Worldwide, email: 76.4% of online adults (internet users aged 16+) said they used email in the past 30 days (GWI Q2 2026 wave). Excluding China, the figure is 86.6%.
sources.publisher: DataReportal (Simon Kemp; Manochi analysis; We Are Social and Meltwater; data from GWI)
sources.quote: with 76.4 percent of respondents to GWI’s survey answering in the affirmative
sources.notes: The preceding clause reads 'online adults say that they’ve used email within the past 30 days'. The wave is named: 'Q2 2026 wave of research'. In text, only Nigeria (98.4%), South Africa (above 95%) and Brazil (94.7%) get country values. The email-by-country chart is an image, and Indonesia is not named in the text. GWI covers about 54 markets, not the whole world, and cannot survey Russia because of sanctions. GWI owns the data; DataReportal is the licensed publisher.

sources.fact: Worldwide, WhatsApp: 54.9% of internet users aged 16+ said they used WhatsApp in the past 30 days (GWI 'latest survey'). That ranks it fourth, after Facebook (58.1%), Instagram (56.6%) and YouTube (56.2%).
sources.publisher: DataReportal (Simon Kemp; Manochi analysis; data from GWI)
sources.quote: and WhatsApp claims fourth place, with 54.9 percent
sources.notes: The base comes from the sentence before: Instagram's 56.6 percent 'of internet users aged 16 and above' who used it 'within the past 30 days'. This paragraph does not name a GWI wave; the email figure in the same report says Q2 2026. Two separate fetches confirmed 54.9%, but the search index has not picked it up yet (it still shows 54% from the 2025 wave). GWI's sample includes China, where WhatsApp is blocked, so the global share is lower than it would otherwise be. The same report's monthly-active ranking is a Similarweb index with WhatsApp at 100, not a user count.

sources.fact: Worldwide, by category: 94.1% of internet users aged 16+ used chat and messaging services such as WhatsApp and Telegram in the past 30 days, against 76.4% who used at least one email service in the past month (GWI).
sources.quote: Chat and messaging services like WhatsApp and Telegram rank second, with 94.1 percent
sources.notes: The email line on this page: 'Email services rank fourth', with 76.4 percent of online adults 'using at least one email service during the past month'. No wave is given for this ranking. These are category figures (they include apps such as WeChat), not WhatsApp alone.

sources.fact: Earlier GWI reading (April 2026 update): email 74.4% of online adults; WhatsApp 54.4% (GWI Q4 2025 wave); WhatsApp 69.8% when China and Russia are excluded.
sources.publisher: DataReportal (Simon Kemp; Manochi; data from GWI)
sources.date: 2026-04 (no explicit date on the page; covers data at the start of April 2026)

sources.fact: DataReportal reuse terms: individual report pages may be republished with clear attribution to DataReportal and the report partners and a link to the report page. Use must count as fair dealing; you may not charge for access or distort the data. Email them before republishing or recreating ten or more pages or charts, or before republishing content from their analysis articles or blog posts. Paid publications pay a fee. Raw data is not provided.
sources.quote: You must include clear attribution to DataReportal and the report partner(s)
sources.notes: No Creative Commons or other open licence; the content is described as the intellectual property of Kepios Pte. Ltd. Recommended citation: <Report Sponsors> (<report year>), '<Report Title>', retrieved from <report page URL> on <date>. The page does not say whether you may quote single data points or draw your own chart from them, and it says nothing about third-party data such as GWI's. datareportal.com/legal adds that all site content is protected by copyright. Contact address seen in a page footer: reports@kepios.com.

sources.fact: GWI's citation guidance: when citing figures from existing reports, saying 'GWI says' or 'GWI data shows' is enough, and you may copy the report's own sourcing line.
sources.quote: you can simply state 'GWI says'/'GWI data shows'
sources.notes: No explicit rule on redistribution or commercial use. Data that is not public (platform-only) needs approval from an account manager. The page also says GWI does not support using its data to criticise, or to harm, another organisation. That matters if the Outlook outage post frames email figures as criticism of Microsoft, though the clause's scope is unclear.

disagreements:
1) WhatsApp worldwide: Meta has given three figures that are not interchangeable. (a) 'more than 3 billion monthly actives' (Zuckerberg, 30 April 2025, from transcript copies). (b) 'More than 3 billion people in over 180 countries' (WhatsApp site, undated, no time window: 'people', not 'monthly actives'). (c) 'more than 2 billion daily actives' (28 January 2026, for the end of 2025). Meta has not restated the monthly figure since April 2025, and in Q1 2026 it reported a Russian restriction on WhatsApp access, so the 3 billion monthly floor may be out of date. Third-party estimates (about 3.3 billion in 2026 from Timelines.ai and Resourcera via Infobip; about 2.9 billion elsewhere) are not Meta figures and contradict each other. GWI's 54.9% of internet users aged 16+ cannot be converted into Meta's count without assumptions: GWI leaves out under-16s, covers only about 54 markets, includes China and does not survey Russia.
2) Email worldwide counts: Radicati gives 4,594 million (2025) and a 4,730 million forecast for 2026. cloudHQ gives 4.83 billion (2025) and 5.02 billion (2026), about 240 to 290 million higher. Secondary sites mix up Radicati's numbers: one attributes 5.02 billion for 2028 to Radicati, one article uses both 4.48 and 4.59 billion for 2024, another cites 4.85 billion by 2027 from an older edition. Radicati's own wording also varies: 'top 4.4' (executive summary, per search), 'over 4.4 billion' (press release), and '4.48 billion' in secondary sources.
3) The GWI email share moves between DataReportal releases: 75% (February 2025), 74.4% (April 2026 update), 76.4% (October 2026, Q2 2026 wave). Waves changed, and GWI added ages 65+ after Q1 2024, so this is not a clean trend. The exclusion sets also differ: email's 86.6% excludes China only, while WhatsApp's 69.8% (April 2026) excludes China and Russia. Do not pair them.
4) Age base: the task's 'aged 16 to 64' is out of date. Current DataReportal and GWI figures use 'internet users aged 16 and above'.
5) WhatsApp in Indonesia: 92.7% (GWI Q2 2026: used in the past month, aged 16+) versus APJII 2026's 1.7% (named as the social platform accessed most often, aged 13+). Search results also show an older APJII 98.07% for chat apps (year unclear), Jakpat's 89% (past six months, 2025), and a secondary 90.8% attributed to Digital 2026 Indonesia (not verified on DataReportal). These answer different questions, but readers could take them as contradictions.
6) Indonesia internet users: DataReportal says 231 million and 80.2% (October 2026, though the text also says 'end of 2026'), with a UN population of 288 million. APJII says 235.26 million and 81.72% (fieldwork February to March 2026, population 287.88 million; another outlet gives 287,303,234, per search). A search snippet gives BPS 2024 as 72.78% of residents aged 5+.
7) Email in Indonesia: BPS 2024 says 12.89% of internet users accessed email. APJII 2025 says 4.20% gave 'using email/communicating' as their main reason. Kominfo and Katadata (2021) found 42.8% had never used email, so about 57% had (my arithmetic, not a published figure). Ipsos reported about 91% (undated, search only). The gaps come from different question designs (main purpose, any use, ever used) and age bases (5+, 13+, 13 to 70).
8) DataReportal attribution: pages credit the analysis to Manochi, while the copyright notice and citation page name Kepios Pte. Ltd. A search snippet of DataReportal's About page says the Kepios team produces the reports.
9) Radicati report date: the PDFs sit in an October 2024 upload folder, but the brochure says 'Copyright © December 2024' and the press release is dated December 2024.
10) Meta Q4 2025 transcript copies differ: the Motley Fool transcript has no WhatsApp daily figure, while VectorShift places it in Zuckerberg's prepared remarks. My inference is that the line comes from the separately published prepared remarks, so cite those.

chart_feasibility:
The pair that can honestly sit side by side is worldwide email at 76.4% against WhatsApp at 54.9%. Both come from the same report (DataReportal Digital 2027 Global Overview, 21 October 2026) and the same survey (GWI), with the same base (internet users aged 16+) and the same window (past 30 days). Suggested label: '% of internet users aged 16+ who used it in the past month, GWI survey via DataReportal, 2026'. Footnote the wave: Q2 2026 is stated for email but not named for WhatsApp. Caveats: the figures are self-reported, cover about 54 markets, include China (where WhatsApp is blocked, which lowers its share) and exclude Russia. A category-level alternative from the same family is chat and messaging services at 94.1% against email services at 76.4% (DataReportal, 'Internet Use Around the World', 21 October 2026). That answers 'messaging versus email', not WhatsApp specifically.
Indonesia: WhatsApp at 92.7% (GWI Q2 2026, aged 16+, monthly) has no email figure on the same basis. Do not set it beside BPS 12.89%, APJII 4.20% or the 2021 Kominfo/Katadata data: the questions, age bases and years all differ, and that chart would mislead.
Counts: putting Radicati's roughly 4.6 billion email users (2025) next to Meta's 'more than 3 billion monthly actives' (April 2025) as bars is not recommended. One is a modelled forecast and the other is a company floor; 'users' differ from 'monthly actives' (possibly accounts); the Radicati figures are unverified here; and Radicati's policy may require permission for non-media use. Never pair the 2 billion daily figure with any monthly figure, never put a count and a percentage on one axis, and leave the WhatsApp logo out (WhatsApp's terms restrict use of its logos and trademarks).
Permissions: DataReportal asks for attribution to DataReportal and its partners (We Are Social, Meltwater), a link to the report page and fair-dealing use, with an email first if ten or more charts are recreated. GWI asks only for 'GWI data shows', but note its clause against using its data to criticise another organisation. For Radicati, email admin@radicati.com before quoting.
Owner decision, multiple choice:
(A) Worldwide GWI pair only: email 76.4% against WhatsApp 54.9%. Recommended.
(B) Option A plus a separate, clearly labelled Indonesia WhatsApp bar at 92.7%, noting that no comparable Indonesia email figure is published.
(C) Category pair instead: chat and messaging 94.1% against email 76.4%.
(D) No chart; state the counts in text only (Radicati's 2025 forecast and Meta's April 2025 floor), each with its own definition.
